searchDocs.title: Method 1 - HTTP request in the Studio console​
searchDocs.content: In Roblox Studio, select the folder where you keep your third party modules / utilities.Run this in the command bar:  local HttpService = game:GetService("HttpService") local Selection = game:GetService("Selection") local parent = Selection:Get()[1] or game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage") local function createModule(name, url) local module = Instance.new("ModuleScript") module.Name = name module.Source = HttpService:GetAsync(url) module.Parent = parent return module end local baseUrl = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Dyscarn/Dysconnect/refs/heads/main/src/" local main = createModule("Dysconnect", `{baseUrl}init.luau`) createModule("DataTypes", `{baseUrl}DataTypes.luau`).Parent = main

searchDocs.title: Method 2 - Manual​
searchDocs.content: Visit the latest release.  Under Assets, download the Dysconnect release file, if one is provided.  Choose the method that matches your workflow:  Using sync tools like Rojo or Argon? Add the downloaded file to your project and update your Rojo configuration as needed.  Using Roblox Studio? Drop the file into the workspace and move it somewhere under ReplicatedStorage.

searchDocs.title: Method 3 - Git Submodule​
searchDocs.content: Add the Dysconnect repository as a Git submodule, ideally inside a folder named submodules.  Update your sync tool project configuration to include the module.  Sync your project with Roblox Studio.

searchDocs.title: Method 4 - Package Manager​
searchDocs.content: Dysconnect currently supports Wally. For support in other package managers, contact Dyscarn in the Discord (top-right) or open a request issue in GitHub.

searchDocs.title: Getting Started with Dysconnect
searchDocs.content: Getting Started with Dysconnect Based on Promise's docs Here are some quick links to get started using Dysconnect: Installation guideAPI DocsUsage & Examples

searchDocs.title: Connection​
searchDocs.content: </> interface Connection { Connected: boolean-- If this Connection is still bound to its event. Type: EventType-- The type of event it's connected to. Name: string-- The name of the event it's connected to. Callback: Callback-- The callback that'll execute when this connection receives a signal. }

searchDocs.title: Disconnect​
searchDocs.content: </> Connection.Disconnect(self: Connection) → () Destroys this Connection, rendering it unusuable and setting its Connection.Connected property to false.

searchDocs.title: Destroy​
searchDocs.content: </> Connection.Destroy(self: Connection) → () Equivalent to Connection.Disconnect.

searchDocs.title: Initialization​
searchDocs.content: Before using Dysconnect, you need to initialize it on both the server and the client.  First, place the Dysconnect ModuleScript and its DataTypes submodule in ReplicatedStorage, preserving the hierarchy expected by your module.  Create a Script inside ServerScriptService:  local Dysconnect = require(game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage").Dysconnect) Dysconnect.Init()   Then, create a LocalScript inside StarterPlayerScripts:  local Dysconnect = require(game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage").Dysconnect) Dysconnect.Init()   Calling Init() sets up the networking instances and connections for the current environment. You should initialize the module once in each environment before using it.

searchDocs.title: Creating a connection​
searchDocs.content: Connections are registered with SetConnection(). Each connection has a name, a type, and a callback that runs when the connection is fired.  For example, register a connection on the server:  Dysconnect.SetConnection("PrintMessage", "REMOTE_EVENT", function(player: Player, message: string) print(player.Name .. " sent:", message) end)   The first argument is the connection's name, "REMOTE_EVENT" specifies the type, and the callback receives the arguments sent with the event. On the server, the callback's first parameter is always the Player who fired the remote.

searchDocs.title: Firing a connection​
searchDocs.content: Once a connection is registered, you can fire it from the other side using FireServerConnection() or FireClientConnection().  For example, in a LocalScript, send a message to the server:  Dysconnect.FireServerConnection("PrintMessage", "REMOTE_EVENT", "Hello from the client!")   The server's registered callback will receive "Hello from the client!" as its message argument.  To send a message from the server to a specific client, use FireClientConnection():  Dysconnect.FireClientConnection(player, "DisplayMessage", "REMOTE_EVENT", "Hello from the server!")   Register the corresponding connection in the client:  Dysconnect.SetConnection("DisplayMessage", "REMOTE_EVENT", function(message: string) print(message) end)   Notice that the target Player is the first argument to FireClientConnection(), before the connection name and type.

searchDocs.title: Broadcasting to all clients​
searchDocs.content: Use FireAllClientConnection() to send a remote event to every connected client.  On the server:  Dysconnect.FireAllClientConnection("RoundStarted", "REMOTE_EVENT", "The round has started!")   On each client:  Dysconnect.SetConnection("RoundStarted", "REMOTE_EVENT", function(message: string) print(message) end)   You can use "UREMOTE_EVENT" instead of "REMOTE_EVENT" when unreliable delivery is appropriate.

searchDocs.title: Remote functions​
searchDocs.content: Remote functions allow the caller to receive return values from the other side.  Register a remote function on the server:  Dysconnect.SetConnection("GetPlayerLevel", "REMOTE_FUNCTION", function(player: Player): number -- Replace this with your own level lookup. return 10 end)   Then invoke it from a LocalScript:  local level = Dysconnect.FireServerConnection("GetPlayerLevel", "REMOTE_FUNCTION") print("Your level is:", level)   The value returned by the server callback is returned to the client. Remote function calls yield while waiting for the other side, so use them when a response is actually needed.  You can also invoke a client from the server with FireClientConnection():  local setting = Dysconnect.FireClientConnection( player, "GetClientSetting", "REMOTE_FUNCTION", "MusicEnabled" )   The client must register the corresponding connection using SetConnection().

searchDocs.title: Unreliable remote events​
searchDocs.content: Use "UREMOTE_EVENT" for frequent updates where occasional packet loss is acceptable, such as cosmetic effects or rapidly changing visual information.  On the client:  Dysconnect.FireServerConnection("UpdateAimDirection", "UREMOTE_EVENT", Vector3.new(0, 0, -1))   On the server:  Dysconnect.SetConnection("UpdateAimDirection", "UREMOTE_EVENT", function(player: Player, direction: Vector3) print(player.Name, direction) end)   Unreliable events aren't suitable for important actions that must reliably arrive, such as purchases or critical state changes.  They should be most commonly used for VFX and repeated debug logs or visualizers.

searchDocs.title: Bindable events​
searchDocs.content: Use "BINDABLE_EVENT" for communication within the same environment. Bindable events do not communicate between the client and server.  IMPORTANT: Most of the times it's better to use ModuleScripts for this with callbacks or something like Signal, but for people that find those confusing, BindableEvents are a decent option.  Register the connection:  Dysconnect.SetConnection("PlayerReady", "BINDABLE_EVENT", function(playerName: string) print(playerName .. " is ready!") end)   Fire it from another script in the same environment:  Dysconnect.FireConnection("PlayerReady", "MyPlayer")   Unlike remote event firing methods, FireConnection() does not require a connection type argument.

searchDocs.title: Sequential arguments and supported data types​
searchDocs.content: Dysconnect lets you pass arguments sequentially instead of wrapping them in a table, like any normal event. Supported values include strings, buffers, and various Roblox data types.  For example, send several values in one event:  Dysconnect.FireAllClientConnection( "UpdateEffect", "REMOTE_EVENT", Vector3.new(10, 5, 20), Color3.fromRGB(255, 100, 50), CFrame.new(0, 5, 0) )   Receive them in the same order:  Dysconnect.SetConnection("UpdateEffect", "REMOTE_EVENT", function(position: Vector3, color: Color3, transform: CFrame) print(position, color, transform) end)   The callback receives the values in the order they were sent. Values that aren't officially supported by Dysconnect's optimized serialization system may fall back to JSON serialization, depending on their type.

searchDocs.title: Connection predicates​
searchDocs.content: SetConnection() accepts an optional predicate as its fourth argument. The callback only runs when the predicate returns true.  Dysconnect.SetConnection( "SubmitScore", "REMOTE_EVENT", function(player: Player, score: number) print(player.Name .. " submitted a score of " .. score) end, function(player: Player, score: number): boolean return score >= 0 and score <= 100000 end )   On server-side remote connections, the predicate also receives the sending Player as its first argument.  Predicates are useful for basic checks, but they don't replace server-side validation of important gameplay actions.

searchDocs.title: Disconnecting a connection​
searchDocs.content: SetConnection() returns a connection object. Call Disconnect() when you no longer need the callback.  local connection = Dysconnect.SetConnection("TemporaryMessage", "BINDABLE_EVENT", function(message: string) print(message) end) Dysconnect.FireConnection("TemporaryMessage", "This will be printed.") connection:Disconnect() Dysconnect.FireConnection("TemporaryMessage", "The disconnected callback will no longer run.")   You can also call connection:Destroy(), which is equivalent to Disconnect().

searchDocs.title: Predicate​
searchDocs.content: </> type Predicate = ((...any) → boolean) | (( Player: Player , ...any ) → boolean) Function containing sanity checks to execute a callback afterwards if it returns true.

searchDocs.title: RemoteType​
searchDocs.content: </> type RemoteType = "REMOTE_EVENT" | "UREMOTE_EVENT" Event types that go over the network and don't return anything.

searchDocs.title: NetworkEventType​
searchDocs.content: </> type NetworkEventType = RemoteType | "BINDABLE_EVENT" Event types that do and don't go over the network but don't return anything.

searchDocs.title: InvokableType​
searchDocs.content: </> type InvokableType = RemoteType | "REMOTE_FUNCTION" Event types that go over the network that do and don't return anything.

searchDocs.title: EventType​
searchDocs.content: </> type EventType = RemoteType | NetworkEventType | InvokableType All supported event and function types in Dysconnect.

searchDocs.title: Init​
searchDocs.content: </> Dysconnect.Init( DebugConfig: DEBUG?,-- Read DEBUG. ExhaustionDetectionConfig: EXHAUSTION_DETECTION?-- Read EXHAUSTION_DETECTION. ) → () Initializes the networking system in the current environment.

searchDocs.title: SetConnection​
searchDocs.content: </> Dysconnect.SetConnection( name: string,-- The name of the instance. Type: EventType,-- The type of the instance. Callback: Callback,-- The code that will run when the connection is fired. Predicate: Predicate ) → Connection-- The set connection for further usage and cleanup.
type Callback = ((...any) → any?) | (( Player: Player , ...any ) → any?)  Adds a connection to a specific event / function instance.

searchDocs.title: FireClientConnection​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the server. Server </> Dysconnect.FireClientConnection( target: Player ,-- The target client whose connections will be fired. name: string,-- The name of the desired event / function. Type: InvokableType,-- The type of instance to fire the connections of. ...: any-- Any arguments to pass to the event. ) → any | nil-- If a RemoteFunction is invoked using this, its returned values will be returned here. Fires a specific client's event / function connections.

searchDocs.title: FireAllClientConnection​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the server. Server </> Dysconnect.FireAllClientConnection( name: string,-- The name of the desired event. Type: RemoteType,-- The type of the event (Reliable / Unreliable). ...: any-- Any arguments to pass to the event. ) → () Fires an event's connections to every single connected client. If the type of the object is a RemoteFunction, it won't do anything.

searchDocs.title: FireServerConnection​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the client. Client </> Dysconnect.FireServerConnection( name: string,-- The name of the desired event / function. Type: InvokableType,-- The type of instance to fire the connections of. ...: any-- Any arguments to pass to the event. ) → any | nil-- If a RemoteFunction is invoked using this, its returned values will be returned here. Fires a connection on the server.

searchDocs.title: FireConnection​
searchDocs.content: </> Dysconnect.FireConnection( name: string,-- The name of the desired BindableEvent. ...: any-- Any arguments to pass to the event. ) → () Fires a BindableEvent's connections.

searchDocs.title: WaitForInit​
searchDocs.content: </> Dysconnect.WaitForInit() → () Yields until the networking service is live for usage.

searchDocs.title: IsLive​
searchDocs.content: </> Dysconnect.IsLive() → boolean-- If the network service is available in the current environment. Checks if this service is available.
